market.summary: Egypt combines a national academic union (EULC/Future), large national and Bibliotheca Alexandrina collections, public lending via MPL, independent university catalogs and international research libraries. Public access differs sharply from catalog visibility. Koha is repeatedly evidenced, but this feasibility-selected sample does not establish national LMS market share.
market.platform_strategy: Highest institutional reach: establish a reliable authorized EULC/Future interface with institution-attributed physical holdings. Highest near-term reuse: Koha, beginning Cairo Law only as a tested research candidate; many large Koha origins explicitly exclude automated search. MPL is a public-lending priority after service/policy verification. BA custom OPAC, OCLC WMS, Diamond-ILS and VuFind require separate endpoint/parser assessment; no product connector is certified.

limitations: No national largest-ten ranking established. Different dates, units, capacity, doctoral theses, catalog titles and printed volumes are not comparable.

Only one substantial selected target and two smaller reserves returned actual book-query records. Twenty-seven blocked/unverified entries are retained; shared EULC origins are not separate institutions.
Robots404 is no published rule, not reuse permission. BA ordinary HTML robots is unknown policy and its bounded query failed.
No login, transaction, hold, outreach, crawling, TLS bypass or production/app change. No live MyBookshelf integration tested.
Failed checks never imply not held. Available items may be reference-only under institution rules; NVIC explicitly forbids borrowing.
Indexed official metrics at Universities of Canada are unvalidated dynamic counts, not current live statistics.
Some source excerpts were retrieved through web discovery; raw catalog responses and request metadata are retained separately.
